findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored without enforced default encryption with a managed KMS key.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or explicit private ACL/bucket policy is defined for this bucket, and no ACL is set at all, leaving exposure to accidental public ACLs or policies.
The bucket that holds report data has no logging block, so unauthorised access to objects such as the vendor roster cannot be detected or investigated.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be overwritten or the whole bucket destroyed with no recoverable prior versions, aiding destructive tampering.
The ledger export bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial exports are stored without enforced default encryption.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, leaving no audit trail of access to ledger export data.
The bucket relies only on a private ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so a later policy or ACL change could expose ledger data publicly.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so model artifacts are stored without enforced default server-side encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public ACLs or policies on this bucket.
The runbooks bucket, which commonly contains operational procedures and sometimes embedded credentials or internal endpoints, has no default server-side encryption configured.
No logging block is configured, so access to operational runbooks is not recorded for audit or incident response.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, leaving it open to accidental public exposure via ACL or policy changes.

The ACL is set to the malformed value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" rather than "log-delivery-write" or "private"; a canned ACL that grants write access to the log delivery group (or an unintended grant from a mistyped value) on the audit log bucket weakens the integrity of audit records.
The central audit log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so public ACLs or bucket policies could expose audit logs of all other buckets.
force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket allows all audit evidence to be deleted in a single terraform destroy, and no object lock / MFA delete protects log integrity.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party PII/contact data) is uploaded into a bucket with no default encryption and no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument set on the object itself.
